column1: # Loop Studio queue-lock reclaim parity table
# `~/.lac/locks/loop-studio-tasks` is taken by two implementations of one rule: the
# Rust one in `common::lock_is_reclaimable` (used by `loop-studio worker`, `loop-studio loop`)
# and the Swift one in `LoopsStore.lockIsReclaimable` (used by the Studio).
# They cannot call each other — Swift and Rust, one filesystem — so instead both
# test suites read THIS file and assert the same verdicts. A change to one
# implementation that the other does not share fails that other's gate, which
# is what turns "kept in sync by hand" into "provably the same rule".
# This file is tracked by `make delivery-index`; a test that reads it fails if
# it is missing.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   case        a name for the row, for a failure message
#   owner       the record in the lock directory: `-` absent, empty = the
#               empty-file window between O_TRUNC and the write
#   dir_age     seconds since the lock directory was last modified, or `-` when
#               the age could not be determined
#   probe       the liveness probe's answer: alive | dead | unprobeable
#   expect      reclaim | keep
# The rule, for reference: the only unconditional reclaim is a pid that is
# provably gone. A live owner keeps the lock regardless of age. Everything else
# — no record, an empty record, an unparsable one, a pid that cannot be probed
# — waits out the backstop (30s), which is what the empty-record window needs.
# --- no record at all: only the backstop may reclaim -------------------------
no-record-fresh
no-record-at-backstop
no-record-aged
no-record-unknown-age
# --- the O_TRUNC window: the file exists and is empty -------------------------
empty-record-fresh
empty-record-at-backstop
garbage-record-fresh
garbage-record-at-backstop
negative-pid-fresh
negative-pid-aged
# --- a real owner, in the format the CLI writes -------------------------------
live-owner-ancient
live-owner-just-born
dead-owner-fresh
dead-owner-ancient
unprobeable-fresh
unprobeable-just-under
unprobeable-at-backstop
# --- the legacy pid-only record the Studio used to write ----------------------
legacy-live-owner
legacy-dead-owner
